title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases involving Computer Network Domain Names

articles.content_en: Article 1: For civil disputes involving the registration, use, and other acts of computer network domain names, where a party institutes a civil action in the People's Court, and upon examination it meets the provisions of Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 2: Cases of domain name infringement disputes shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intermediate People's Court of the place where the infringing act is committed or where the defendant is domiciled. Where it is difficult to determine the place of the infringing act and the place where the defendant is domiciled, the place where the computer terminal or other equipment by which the plaintiff discovers the domain name is located may be deemed the place of the infringing act.
Foreign-related domain name dispute cases include those in which one or both parties are foreigners, stateless persons, foreign enterprises or organizations, or international organizations, or where the domain name is registered abroad. For foreign-related domain name dispute cases occurring within the territory of the People's Republic of China, jurisdiction shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of Part IV of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 3: The cause of action of a domain name dispute case shall be determined based on the nature of the legal relationship in dispute between the parties, and shall be preceded by the words "computer network domain name". Where the nature of the legal relationship in dispute is difficult to determine, it may be generally referred to as a computer network domain name dispute case.

Article 6: When hearing a domain name dispute case, the People's Court may, at the request of the party and according to the specific circumstances of the case, determine in accordance with law whether the involved registered trademark is well-known.

Article 7: Where the People's Court determines that the registration, use, or other acts of a domain name constitute infringement or unfair competition, it may order the defendant to cease the infringement and cancel the domain name, or, at the request of the plaintiff, order that the domain name be registered and used by the plaintiff; where actual damage is caused to the right holder, it may order the defendant to compensate for losses.
Where the infringer intentionally infringes and the circumstances are serious, the plaintiff has the right to request punitive damages from the People's Court.
